trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
The line must go right: up is number 8, which comes later.
Cell (5,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
I can't rule out up or right yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.
Cell (1,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going up, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,4); going right would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order). So my guess (up from cell (2,2)) was wrong, so the line must go right.
Going down, the next 7 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,4). So the line goes up.
Cell (1,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going right would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order). So the line goes down.
Cell (4,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going right, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,5); going to number 4, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes down.
Going right would leave both cell (4,6) and number 7 needing the line next, and it can't do both; going down would force the line onto number 7 before its turn. So the line goes left.
Cell (4,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going right would cut off the top-right corner (6 cells). So the line goes up.

Going up would leave both cell (1,4) and number 6 needing the line next, and it can't do both; going right would leave both number 6 and cell (3,6) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
